subject.title: feat: expose readable session presentation metadata

question: Should the permanent Gateway presentation contract contain a closed registry of optional subsystem/plugin session families, or should core expose generic families plus owner-provided presentation metadata?
rationale: Both designs can produce readable clients, but only maintainers can choose the long-term protocol ownership and compatibility model for future plugins and native clients.

options.title: Use an extensible owner seam
options.body: Keep generic core families and let the owning plugin or prepared session metadata supply a namespaced family/title/background projection without adding every optional family to the core enum.

options.title: Adopt a core registry
options.body: Accept the closed core family registry, document its stability guarantees, and add compatibility tests and an explicit process for adding or retiring families.

options.title: Narrow to generic metadata
options.body: Ship only title, subtitle, main/background, agent, channel, and account fields now, deferring detailed family taxonomy until the ownership contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Use an extensible owner seam
recommendation.body: Keep generic core families and let the owning plugin or prepared session metadata supply a namespaced family/title/background projection without adding every optional family to the core enum.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-picker and session-presentation work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-client contract decision.
